objective: Harden trusted AI access session issuance so unsafe actor and scope identifiers are rejected before any signed AI access headers are created.

codeReferences.summary: Trusted-session issuance now validates the trimmed actor id with the shared safe-id guard before signing claims.
Scope normalization now rejects unsafe scope ids before compacted claims can be signed.
Regression proves unsafe trusted actor ids are rejected during issuance.
Regression proves unsafe trusted scope ids are rejected during issuance.

redGreenEvidence.observedFailure: The unsafe actor-id and unsafe scope-id issuance tests both failed because createUaisAiAccessSessionForTrustedActor did not throw before signing.

redGreenEvidence.observedPass: 3 focused tests passed, including the pre-existing missing-secret assertion and the two new unsafe-id issuance assertions.

verification.summary: 4 focused production release-gate direct-call tests passed.
Next.js production build completed with exit code 0.

securityPosture.issuerBoundary: Trusted AI access session issuance now fails before producing signed headers when actor or scope identifiers are unsafe.
securityPosture.parserBoundary: Existing signed-session parsing still rejects unsafe actor and scope identifiers if a malformed signed claim is received.
securityPosture.requestResourceBoundary: Existing signed-session resource validation still rejects unsafe request resource identifiers before scope authorization.
securityPosture.redaction: The new errors are generic and do not echo path-like identifiers or signing secrets.

aggregateEnterpriseGateImpact.summary: This narrows the AI direct-call contract risk by moving unsafe-id rejection earlier in the signed-session lifecycle. The full enterprise gate still requires same-run owner-approved production evidence for env placement, deployment, storage, ordinary teaching route/browser smokes, app-auth readiness, browser workflow smoke, and live provider generation.
